summary: Implemented the IntervalSeconds model-level guard in ThumbnailGenerationRequest and all related deliverables: (1) Added ArgumentOutOfRangeException guard to ThumbnailGenerationRequest.cs using positional-record property override pattern — validates at construction time; (2) Added Math.Max(1, IntervalSeconds) clamp + effectiveRequests projection in ThumbnailGeneratorViewModel.Generate() so model guard is never tripped in production; (3) Added System.Diagnostics.Debug.Assert(false, ...) before the existing service-layer clamp in FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs to signal any guard bypass during debugging while retaining the defensive fallback; (4) Created ThumbnailGenerationRequestTests.cs with 3 test cases (zero → throws, negative → throws, one → no throw); (5) Updated api-surface.md ThumbnailGenerationRequest entry to document the guard; also corrected the stale comment about MoviesListViewModel not implementing IDisposable (addressed in WP-001). comments.note: ThumbnailGenerationRequest.cs: The property-initializer guard pattern validates at constructor time but is silently bypassed by `with` expressions (the init accessor is called directly, not the initializer). A custom init accessor body (`set { if (value <= 0) throw ...; _intervalSeconds = value; }`) would close this gap. Since no `with` usages with invalid values exist today, the current pattern is acceptable, but worth documenting as a known limitation.

ThumbnailGeneratorViewModel.cs: The effectiveRequests LINQ projection uses r.with { IntervalSeconds = effectiveInterval } on every call to Generate(). If _requests is large, this creates a new list per generation run. This is negligible for typical movie counts but could be pre-computed or memoized if the interval binding is confirmed stable between sessions.

FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs: The defensive clamp (intervalMs = 30_000L) is now guarded by Debug.Assert but remains reachable code. A future milestone could promote the Debug.Assert to a production-mode guard (throw InvalidOperationException) and remove the clamp entirely, making the invariant a hard contract at all build configurations.

comments.note: ThumbnailGenerationRequest.cs property-initializer guard is idiomatic C# for records. paramName is correct (nameof(IntervalSeconds)), the exception message is clear and includes the actual value. The guard fires on construction via the positional constructor — which is the only path used by application code.

The known with-expression bypass (C# language limitation) is correctly mitigated: ThumbnailGeneratorViewModel applies Math.Max(1, IntervalSeconds) before every with-expression, ensuring the value passed to the init accessor is always >= 1. The Debug.Assert in FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService acts as a belt-and-suspenders signal for any bypass that slips through in debug builds. The layered defense is well-documented in code comments at each layer.

ThumbnailGenerationRequestTests.cs: Three tests are clean and well-named. FluentAssertions .Throw<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>().WithParameterName("IntervalSeconds") validates both exception type and parameter name — strong assertion that correctly rejects misconfigured throws (e.g. if a throw had wrong paramName). .NotThrow() for the valid case is also correct.

FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs Debug.Assert message is clear, includes the movie ID and interval value, and explains the guard bypass scenario. The LogWarning is also retained so a production bypass (e.g. from reflection) is traceable in logs. Good defensive layering.
